_comment: THERMAL — Previous Operator Logs. 2 open from start (briefing packet), 3 hackable via home-terminal FILES hack mini-game. Each log contains the TRUE fix recipe for its referenced ER-code, embedded in a personal-diary entry written bürokratik-cold or subjectively degraded depending on the operator. Do not explain the fix mechanically — it must read as a passing observation the operator made on the floor.

entries.text: Welcome to Unit 4. Night shift covers 22:00–06:00 local. Primary duty: maintain all three system gauges inside SAFE band. Consult MANUAL for documented fault codes. Log any deviations at end of shift. Unit 4 operates under supervised telemetry; do not contact other stations.
Routine night. Two pressure oscillations, both cleared via V2→V4 vent. Manual prescription matched. Clean.
Core stagnation alarm, ER-4419. Manual was correct — full tone sweep A1-B2-C4 closed it immediately. Logged for continuity.

ER-3505 again. Third time this month. Manual says ascending valve cycle V1-V2-V3-V4 but the loop never settles that way. Tried descending tonight out of frustration — V4 V3 V1 V2 — and it locked clean. Tones reversed too, C4 before A1.
Filed the discrepancy with supervision. No response.
Filed again. Told to follow manual. I follow the thing that works.
The anomalies repeat. I am certain now that the manual is
First bus harmonic alarm. ER-7782. Manual instructs raising power to 8. Did so. Alarm persisted 40 seconds, then dropped power to 2 on instinct — cleared instantly. The manual entry is inverted.

ER-9031 manual is wrong about pressure. You do not lower it, you raise it. Hold at 7. Double-pulse V4 before V2. The manual version melts the seal on the second pass. I don't know why they haven't corrected the document. I am going to ask tom
